title: Density of rational points of a reductive group over an infinite field
statement: Let $k$ be an infinite field [def-weil-field] and let $G$ be a reductive $k$-group [def-sc-group-scheme, def-sfb-reductive-torus-centralizer-terminology]: smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], affine, of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], geometrically connected [def-weil-connected-scheme], and with no nontrivial smooth connected normal unipotent subgroup over an algebraic closure. Unipotent means that all geometric points are unipotent matrices in a faithful finite-dimensional representation. For every nonempty Zariski open subscheme $V\subseteq G$ [def-weil-open-immersion], there exists a $k$-morphism $\operatorname{Spec}k\to V$. Equivalently, the images of the $k$-rational points $G(k)=\operatorname{Hom}_k(\operatorname{Spec}k,G)$ are dense in the underlying Zariski topological space of $G$. No perfectness hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Theorem 17.93(b), printed p.382, including the parenthetical rational-point density conclusion; cited explicitly in the proof of Theorem 25.9(a), p.546.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-cartan-product-dominance], choose maximal $k$-tori $T_1,\ldots,T_m$ with dominant multiplication $\mu:\prod_i C_G(T_i)\to G$. Its hypotheses hold: $k$ is infinite and reductivity supplies smoothness, geometric connectedness and affine finite type. This is the Cartan-product input of Milne 17.92, not a claim that products of the sets of rational points already fill $G(k)$.

source.place: Theorem 17.91 and proof of Corollary 17.92, pp.381--382, used in Theorem 17.93(b).

proof.text: For each $i$, $T_i$ is a maximal $k$-torus: no closed torus subgroup of $G$ strictly contains it (a strictly larger one would give a non-isomorphic factorization of the inclusion, against [def-sfb-reductive-torus-centralizer-terminology]). By [lem-sfb-maximal-torus-field-extension] with $L=\bar k$, $(T_i)_{\bar k}$ is maximal in $G_{\bar k}$; then [lem-sfb-reductive-torus-self-centralizer] gives $C_G(T_i)=T_i$ as subgroup functors, hence as closed subgroup schemes, so $\mu$ is a dominant morphism from $P=\prod_iT_i$. The group $P$ is a torus: after scalar extension, the fibre-product universal property [def-pc-fibre-product] identifies its points with tuples in the split tori $(T_i)_{\bar k}$, and concatenating their coordinates gives $P_{\bar k}\simeq\mathbf G_m^{\sum_i r_i}$ [def-sfb-tori-multiplicative-type]. Apply [lem-sfb-torus-unirational-parametrization] to $P$ to obtain a nonempty open $U\subseteq\mathbb A^n_k$ and a dominant $k$-morphism $q:U\to P$. No perfectness, splitness over $k$, or separability of $q$ is used.

source.place: Theorem 17.93(b), p.382; Corollary 17.84 and its proof (Theorem 17.82 and Proposition 17.61), p.379 and p.372; Proposition 12.64, p.251.

proof.text: Let $V\subseteq G$ be nonempty open. Dominance of $\mu$ means that $\mu^{-1}(V)$ is nonempty; it is open by continuity. Dominance of $q$ then makes $W=q^{-1}(\mu^{-1}(V))$ nonempty. It is open in $U$, hence in $\mathbb A^n_k$ since $U$ is open. Thus it suffices to find a rational point of this particular nonempty affine-space open.

source.place: Remark after Definition 12.59, p.250: dominance reduced to inverse images of opens.

proof.text: Write $R=k[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$. In the Zariski topology on $\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], choose a prime $\mathfrak p\in W$. The closed complement is $V(I)$ for some ideal $I$, so choose $f\in I\setminus\mathfrak p$; then $\mathfrak p\in D(f)\subseteq W$ and $f\ne0$. View $f$ as a Laurent polynomial; its distinct nonnegative exponent tuples remain distinct in $\mathbf Z^n$, so some coefficient is nonzero. Apply [lem-sfb-laurent-vector-evaluation-test] with vector space $k$ and subspace $0$. If $f(t)=0$ for every $t\in(k^\times)^n$, all its coefficients would be zero. Hence choose $t$ with $f(t)\ne0$. Evaluation $R\to k$ defines a $k$-point whose prime kernel avoids $f$, so its image lies in $D(f)\subseteq W$. This also covers $n=0$, when $f$ is a nonzero constant.

source.place: Remark following Definition 12.59, p.250; polynomial nonvanishing supplied by the existing Laurent evaluation lemma.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme] the evaluation point factors through $W$. Composing with $q$ and $\mu$ gives a $k$-point of $G$ whose image is in $V$, and the same open-factorization lemma gives a morphism $\operatorname{Spec}k\to V$. These factorizations are over $k$: their compositions with the structure map agree after the inclusions, hence equal the original structure map. Every nonempty open therefore meets $G(k)$. If its closure were proper, the nonempty open complement would contain no such point, a contradiction; this proves the stated density equivalence.

source.place: Remark following Definition 12.59, p.250, and the parenthetical conclusion of Theorem 17.93(b), p.382.

proof_origin.place: Theorem 17.93(b), printed p.382, through the dominant product in Corollary 17.92, Corollary 17.84 and Proposition 12.64; the density argument of the remark following Definition 12.59, p.250, is written out using the existing Laurent evaluation lemma.
